quiz.title: T3.3: Handles Nulls
quiz.description: Test your understanding of $CHAR(0) vs empty string vs SQL NULL, null behavior in SQL queries, IFNULL/COALESCE, and the interplay between ObjectScript and SQL null handling.

questions.question:
Consider the following ObjectScript code:

set a = ""
set b = $CHAR(0)
write a = b
options: 0 (false) - $CHAR(0) is a single character, "" is an empty string
An error because $CHAR(0) is not a valid value
questions.explanation: $CHAR(0) produces a single character (the NUL character, ASCII code 0) with $LENGTH of 1. The empty string "" has $LENGTH of 0. They are different values. In ObjectScript, $CHAR(0) is a valid character that can appear in strings, not a synonym for empty or NULL. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=RCOS_fchar)

questions.question:
A developer sets a property to empty string in ObjectScript and then queries it via SQL:

set obj = ##class(Sample.Person).%OpenId(1)
set obj.Email = ""
set sc = obj.%Save()

// Later, via SQL:
&sql(SELECT COUNT(*) INTO :cnt FROM Sample.Person WHERE Email IS NULL AND ID = 1)
write cnt
options: 0 - the empty string is not NULL in SQL
1 - the empty string in ObjectScript maps to NULL in SQL
An error because you cannot compare empty strings with IS NULL
0 - IS NULL only matches explicit NULL insertions
questions.explanation: In InterSystems IRIS, the ObjectScript empty string "" IS the representation of SQL NULL. Setting a property to "" (or leaving it unset, since "" is the default) projects as SQL NULL, so IS NULL matches the row and cnt = 1. The SQL zero-length string '' is the ObjectScript value $CHAR(0), which is a distinct value of length 1 and does NOT match IS NULL (it matches = ''). (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GSQL_langelements#GSQL_langelements_null)

questions.question:
Consider the following ObjectScript code:

set x = $CHAR(0)
write $LENGTH(x), " "
write $ASCII(x), " "
write x = "", " "
write $LENGTH(""), " "
write $ASCII("")
questions.explanation: $CHAR(0) has $LENGTH = 1 (it is one character). $ASCII($CHAR(0)) = 0 (the NUL character's ASCII code). $CHAR(0) = "" is 0 (false, they are different). $LENGTH("") = 0 (empty string). $ASCII("") = -1 (the special return value for an empty string). These distinctions are critical for understanding null handling. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=RCOS_fchar)

questions.question:
A table has three rows inserted as follows:

&sql(INSERT INTO Sample.Test (Code) VALUES ('ABC'))
&sql(INSERT INTO Sample.Test (Code) VALUES (''))
&sql(INSERT INTO Sample.Test (Code) VALUES (NULL))

Now consider these two queries:

Query A: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Sample.Test WHERE Code IS NULL
Query B: SELECT COUNT(Code) FROM Sample.Test

What are the results of Query A and Query B?
questions.explanation: In InterSystems IRIS, SQL '' (zero-length string) and SQL NULL are different values. Inserting '' stores the ObjectScript value $CHAR(0) (a non-NULL, length-1 value); inserting NULL stores the ObjectScript empty string "" (which is how IRIS represents SQL NULL). Query A: only the explicit NULL row matches IS NULL, so count = 1. Query B: COUNT(Code) counts non-NULL values — both 'ABC' and '' are non-NULL, so count = 2. Note: COUNT(*) would return 3 (all rows). (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GSQL_langelements#GSQL_langelements_null)

In ObjectScript, the if command evaluates expressions numerically. The empty string "" has numeric value 0, so it is falsy. $CHAR(0) also has numeric value 0 (it is a string that does not begin with a digit), so it is also falsy. Both produce "falsy". Even though they are different values ($LENGTH-wise), they share the same numeric coercion to 0. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GCOS_operators)

questions.question:
A developer writes a SQL query with COALESCE:

&sql(SELECT COALESCE(Phone, Email, 'No Contact') INTO :contact
     FROM Sample.Person WHERE ID = :id)

If the row has Phone = '' and Email = 'user@test.com', what value does :contact hold?
questions.explanation: In InterSystems IRIS, SQL '' (zero-length string) is NOT the same as SQL NULL. COALESCE returns the first non-NULL argument. Since Phone = '' is a zero-length string (not NULL), COALESCE returns '' immediately without checking Email or the fallback. To make COALESCE skip Phone, it would need to be NULL (represented in ObjectScript by the empty string ""), not the SQL zero-length string (represented in ObjectScript by $CHAR(0)). (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=RSQL_coalesce)

questions.question:
Consider the following table and query:

&sql(INSERT INTO Sample.Exam (Score) VALUES (10))
&sql(INSERT INTO Sample.Exam (Score) VALUES (NULL))
&sql(INSERT INTO Sample.Exam (Score) VALUES (20))
&sql(INSERT INTO Sample.Exam (Score) VALUES (NULL))
&sql(INSERT INTO Sample.Exam (Score) VALUES (30))

&sql(SELECT AVG(Score) INTO :avg,
            SUM(Score) INTO :total,
            COUNT(Score) INTO :cnt,
            COUNT(*) INTO :allRows
     FROM Sample.Exam)

write avg, " ", total, " ", cnt, " ", allRows
questions.explanation: SQL aggregate functions (except COUNT(*)) ignore NULL values. SUM(Score) = 10+20+30 = 60. COUNT(Score) = 3 (non-NULL values only). AVG(Score) = 60/3 = 20. COUNT(*) = 5 (counts all rows regardless of NULL). This is standard SQL behavior - NULL values are excluded from aggregation but COUNT(*) counts rows, not values. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=RSQL_avg)

questions.question:
A developer stores data using $CHAR(0) as a delimiter:

set record = "John" _ $CHAR(0) _ "Doe" _ $CHAR(0) _ "Boston"
write $PIECE(record, $CHAR(0), 2)

What is displayed?
options: An error because $CHAR(0) is not a valid delimiter
questions.explanation: $CHAR(0) is a valid single character (NUL, ASCII 0) and works perfectly as a delimiter in $PIECE. It is commonly used as a delimiter because it rarely appears in actual data. The second piece of the record is "Doe". This demonstrates that $CHAR(0) is a real character, not equivalent to empty string or NULL. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=RCOS_fpiece)

questions.question:
Consider this SQL query using IFNULL:

&sql(SELECT IFNULL(MiddleName, 'N/A') INTO :middle FROM Sample.Person WHERE ID = :id)

The row was inserted with:

&sql(INSERT INTO Sample.Person (Name, MiddleName) VALUES ('John', ''))

What value does :middle hold?
questions.explanation: MiddleName was inserted as the SQL zero-length string '' (stored in ObjectScript as $CHAR(0)), which in InterSystems IRIS is NOT the same as SQL NULL. '' is a valid non-NULL value. IFNULL(MiddleName, 'N/A') returns '' because MiddleName is not NULL — it is a zero-length string. IFNULL only substitutes the fallback when the value IS NULL (represented in ObjectScript by the empty string ""). To get 'N/A', the insert would need VALUES ('John', NULL). (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=RSQL_ifnull)

questions.question:
A developer writes the following ObjectScript code to check for null values:

ClassMethod IsEmpty(val As %String) As %Boolean
{
    if val = "" quit 1
    quit 0
}

write ##class(MyApp.Utils).IsEmpty(""), " "
write ##class(MyApp.Utils).IsEmpty($CHAR(0)), " "
write ##class(MyApp.Utils).IsEmpty(0)
questions.explanation: "" = "" is 1 (true). $CHAR(0) = "" is 0 (false, $CHAR(0) is a different string from empty string). 0 = "" is 0 (false) because the = operator only performs numeric comparison when BOTH operands have numeric values. The empty string "" is not a numeric value, so this is a string comparison: the string "0" does not equal the empty string "". This is a key behavior of ObjectScript's = operator. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GCOS_operators)

questions.question:
Consider a table with nullable columns:

&sql(INSERT INTO Sample.Order (Total, Discount) VALUES (100, NULL))
set id = %ROWID
&sql(SELECT Total - Discount INTO :net FROM Sample.Order WHERE ID = :id)
write net
options: NULL — received as empty string in the host variable
An error because you cannot subtract NULL
questions.explanation: In SQL, any arithmetic operation involving NULL returns NULL. 100 - NULL = NULL. This is standard SQL behavior and applies in InterSystems IRIS as well. When a NULL result is returned into an embedded SQL host variable, it is received as an empty string. To handle this, use COALESCE: Total - COALESCE(Discount, 0). (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GSQL_langelements)

questions.question:
A developer needs to distinguish between a property that was never set and one explicitly set to empty. They write:

set obj1 = ##class(Sample.Person).%New()
set obj1.Email = ""
set sc = obj1.%Save()
set id1 = obj1.%Id()

set obj2 = ##class(Sample.Person).%New()
; Email is NOT set on obj2
set sc = obj2.%Save()
set id2 = obj2.%Id()

&sql(SELECT COUNT(*) INTO :cnt FROM Sample.Person
     WHERE ID IN (:id1, :id2) AND Email IS NULL)
write cnt
options: 1 - only the explicitly set empty string is NULL
1 - only the unset property is NULL
2 - both unset and empty string properties are NULL in SQL
questions.explanation: In InterSystems IRIS, a property that was never set defaults to "" (empty string), and a property explicitly set to "" stores the same value. The ObjectScript empty string IS the representation of SQL NULL, so both rows project as NULL in SQL and both match IS NULL — cnt = 2. Because both paths lead to the same stored value, there is no way at the SQL level to distinguish 'never set' from 'set to empty'. To make a property non-NULL but zero-length, set it to $CHAR(0) (which projects as the SQL zero-length string '', not NULL). (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GSQL_langelements#GSQL_langelements_null)

questions.question:
Consider the following SQL query on a table where some City values are NULL:

&sql(SELECT COUNT(*) INTO :cnt FROM Sample.Person WHERE City <> 'Boston')

The table has 100 rows: 30 have City = 'Boston', 50 have other cities, and 20 have City IS NULL. What is cnt?
options: 70 - all rows that are not Boston (including NULL)
50 - only rows with a non-NULL city that is not Boston
questions.explanation: In SQL, NULL <> 'Boston' evaluates to UNKNOWN (not TRUE). Rows where the comparison evaluates to UNKNOWN are excluded from the result set. Only the 50 rows with an actual non-NULL, non-Boston city satisfy the WHERE clause. To include NULL rows, use: WHERE City <> 'Boston' OR City IS NULL. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GSQL_langelements)

questions.question:
A developer writes a method that processes global data and encounters $CHAR(0):

set ^data(1) = "Hello" _ $CHAR(0) _ "World"
set val = ^data(1)
write $LENGTH(val), " "
write $PIECE(val, $CHAR(0), 1), " "
write $PIECE(val, $CHAR(0), 2)
questions.explanation: $CHAR(0) is a single character, so "Hello" (5) + $CHAR(0) (1) + "World" (5) = 11 characters total. $PIECE with $CHAR(0) delimiter correctly splits the string: piece 1 = "Hello", piece 2 = "World". The NUL character is stored and preserved in globals just like any other character. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=RCOS_fchar)

questions.question:
Consider the following SQL statements:

&sql(CREATE TABLE Sample.NullTest (A VARCHAR(10), B VARCHAR(10)))
&sql(INSERT INTO Sample.NullTest VALUES ('X', NULL))
&sql(INSERT INTO Sample.NullTest VALUES (NULL, 'Y'))
&sql(INSERT INTO Sample.NullTest VALUES (NULL, NULL))

&sql(SELECT COUNT(*) INTO :cnt FROM Sample.NullTest
     WHERE COALESCE(A, B, 'none') = 'none')
write cnt
questions.explanation: COALESCE returns the first non-NULL argument. Row 1: COALESCE('X', NULL, 'none') = 'X'. Row 2: COALESCE(NULL, 'Y', 'none') = 'Y'. Row 3: COALESCE(NULL, NULL, 'none') = 'none'. Only row 3 produces 'none', so cnt = 1. COALESCE is essential for providing fallback values when columns may be NULL. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=RSQL_coalesce)
